Module building

A co-expression module is a group of proteins whose abundances rise and fall together across biopsies. WGCNA (Langfelder and Horvath 2008) finds them, and each module is then summarised by its eigengene: one number per biopsy that follows the module’s shared pattern. Later steps test eigengenes instead of hundreds of single proteins. Module construction never sees a group label or a phenotype.

Packages

library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(WGCNA)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
disableWGCNAThreads()

Input

limpa’s complete matrix with each protein’s blood slope removed. WGCNA takes no covariate and no missing values, so this is the matrix it can use. It inherits the blood-removal problem shown in 03_Quantification for the 85 proteins measured in 20 or fewer runs.

stage <- here("01_Processing", "06_Module_Building")
out <- file.path(stage, "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(corrected = "01_Processing/03_Quantification/c_data/DAList_corrected.rds")
paths <- map_chr(inputs, here)
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
abund <- as.matrix(corrected$data)
meta <- as_tibble(corrected$metadata) |>
  select(sample_id, subject, group, timepoint)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(abund), meta$sample_id))
dim(abund)
[1] 1900   45
count(count(meta, subject, name = "biopsies"), biopsies, name = "people")

  biopsies people
     <int>  <int>
1        1      1
2        2      1

Define modules on within-person variation

WGCNA treats every biopsy as an independent sample. These 45 biopsies come from 16 people measured up to three times, and person identity drives the leading components of the abundance matrix. Left alone, modules would mostly group proteins that differ between people. So the modules are defined on person-centred abundance: each protein’s value minus that person’s mean. A person with a single biopsy centres to zeros and adds nothing, so they are left out of the definition and kept for scoring.

repeated <- meta |>
  add_count(subject) |>
  filter(n > 1)
centred <- t(apply(abund[, repeated$sample_id], 1, \(x) x - ave(x, repeated$subject)))
expr <- t(centred)
one <- repeated$sample_id[repeated$subject == repeated$subject[1]]
rbind(raw = round(abund[1, one], 2), centred = round(centred[1, one], 2))
        S03_T1 S03_T2 S03_T3
raw      25.72  25.48  25.28
centred   0.23  -0.01  -0.21
c(runs_defining = nrow(expr), runs_scored = ncol(abund))
runs_defining   runs_scored 
           44            45

Soft power

WGCNA turns each pair’s correlation into a connection strength by raising it to a power (the soft power): higher powers keep strong links and shrink weak ones. The chosen power is the lowest whose network looks scale-free, meaning a few proteins carry many connections and most carry few, by a fit R² of at least 0.85 (pickSoftThreshold()’s estimate). The WGCNA FAQ’s table for signed networks (12 for over 40 samples) is the fallback if no power reaches it.

Two settings depart from the package defaults, both recommended in the WGCNA FAQ:

  • a signed network, so proteins that move in opposite directions are not linked;
  • biweight midcorrelation (bicor), a correlation that down-weights outlying values, with maxPOutliers = 0.05 (the default of 1 switches that guard off). pearsonFallback uses an ordinary correlation for a protein with zero spread.
bicor_args <- list(corType = "bicor", maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = "individual")
sft <- pickSoftThreshold(expr,
  powerVector = 1:20, networkType = "signed",
  corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = list(maxPOutliers = 0.05), verbose = 0
)

power <- coalesce(sft$powerEstimate, faq_power)
fit_indices <- as_tibble(sft$fitIndices) |>
  mutate(signed_r2 = -sign(slope) * SFT.R.sq, chosen = Power == power)
filter(fit_indices, Power %in% (power + -2:2)) |>
  select(Power, signed_r2, mean.k., chosen)

Modules

blockwiseModules() builds the network, measures how many neighbours each pair shares (the topological overlap, TOM), clusters proteins on it, and merges modules whose eigengenes correlate above 0.85 (mergeCutHeight = 0.15). Proteins that fit no module go to grey. Settings that are not package defaults: minModuleSize = 30 (default min(20, n/2); no recorded evidence for 30) and maxBlockSize = 2500, which keeps all 1,900 proteins in one block. randomSeed seeds the clustering inside the function; a set.seed() outside it would be overridden.

net <- do.call(blockwiseModules, c(
  list(expr,
    power = power, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed",
    deepSplit = 2, minModuleSize = 30, mergeCutHeight = 0.15,
    pamStage = TRUE, pamRespectsDendro = TRUE, maxBlockSize = 2500,
    numericLabels = FALSE, randomSeed = 54321, verbose = 0
  ),
  bicor_args
))
colours <- set_names(net$colors, colnames(expr))
sort(table(colours), decreasing = TRUE)
colours
        grey    turquoise         blue        brown       yellow        green 
         304          285          222          172          137          115 
         red        black         pink      magenta       purple  greenyellow 
         104          100           89           78           58           57 
         tan       salmon         cyan midnightblue 
          54           43           41           41

Eigengenes and membership

The eigengene is the first principal component of a module’s proteins, scored here on the uncentred matrix so that differences between people, and so between HR and LR, stay testable. moduleEigengenes() flips each eigengene’s sign to follow the module’s average abundance (package default).

me <- moduleEigengenes(t(abund), colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
rownames(me) <- colnames(abund)
eigengenes <- t(as.matrix(me))
rownames(eigengenes) <- sub("^ME", "", rownames(eigengenes))
round(eigengenes[1:3, 1:4], 3)
      S03_T1 S10_T1 S16_T1 S22_T1
black -0.178  0.011 -0.108  0.164
blue  -0.316  0.130  0.029 -0.250
brown -0.158  0.073 -0.048 -0.385

A protein’s kME is its correlation with its module’s eigengene: near 1 means it follows the module closely. kME is read on the person-centred data that defined the modules, because on uncentred data the differences between people dilute it.

centred_me <- moduleEigengenes(expr, colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
kme <- signedKME(expr, centred_me,
  corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = 'individual'"
)
colnames(kme) <- sub("^kME", "", colnames(kme))
gene_of <- set_names(corrected$annotation$gene, corrected$annotation$uniprot_id)
membership <- tibble(
  uniprot_id = names(colours), gene = unname(gene_of[names(colours)]), module = unname(colours)
) |>
  mutate(kme = map2_dbl(uniprot_id, module, \(id, m) if (m == "grey") NA_real_ else kme[id, m]))
membership |>
  filter(module != "grey") |>
  slice_max(kme, n = 2, by = module) |>
  arrange(module) |>
  head(6)
# A tibble: 6 × 4
  uniprot_id gene   module   kme

How much each eigengene still depends on the person

The intraclass correlation (ICC) is the share of an eigengene’s variance that lies between people rather than between one person’s biopsies, from a mixed model with time point fitted (lme4, eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject)), so time effects do not count as noise.

eigengene_long <- as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id") |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "module", values_to = "eigengene") |>
  left_join(meta, by = "sample_id")
subject_icc <- eigengene_long |>
  summarise(
    icc = {
      v <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(suppressMessages(
        lme4::lmer(eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject))
      )))$vcov
      v[1] / (v[1] + v[2])
    },
    .by = module
  )
module_summary <- count(filter(membership, module != "grey"), module, name = "n_proteins") |>
  left_join(subject_icc, by = "module") |>
  arrange(desc(n_proteins))
module_summary

module_summary |>
  mutate(module = factor(module, levels = rev(module))) |>
  ggplot(aes(n_proteins, module, fill = module)) +
  geom_col(colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("ICC %.2f", icc)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = module_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(x = "proteins", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
trajectory <- eigengene_long |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(eigengene), se = sd(eigengene) / sqrt(n()),
    .by = c(module, group, timepoint)
  )
ggplot(trajectory, aes(timepoint, mean, colour = group, group = group)) +
  geom_line(
    data = eigengene_long, aes(y = eigengene, group = subject),
    alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), size = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(module, levels = module_summary$module), nrow = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(HR = "#2166AC", LR = "#B2182B"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "eigengene") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

Validation

stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(eigengenes), meta$sample_id),
  setequal(rownames(eigengenes), setdiff(unique(colours), "grey")),
  all(abs(membership$kme[membership$module != "grey"]) <= 1),
  sum(module_summary$n_proteins) + sum(colours == "grey") == nrow(abund)
)

Summary

at_power <- filter(fit_indices, Power == power)

Soft power 11 (signed R² 0.857, mean connectivity 9.5). 15 modules of 41 to 285 proteins; 304 of 1900 proteins fit no module. 44 of 45 runs defined the modules. Module colours are labels only and change if 01_Processing is rebuilt.

Save

modules.rds is read by module characterisation, module contrasts and preservation, classification, the trait steps, proteome clustering and the F2 figure.

saveRDS(
  list(
    eigengenes = eigengenes, membership = membership, meta = meta, module_summary = module_summary
  ),
  file.path(out, "modules.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
sheets <- list(
  module_summary = module_summary, membership = membership,
  eigengenes = as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id"),
  soft_threshold = fit_indices
)
holds <- c(
  "Proteins per module and the subject ICC of its eigengene.",
  "Every protein's module and its kME in that module.",
  "Module eigengene per sample, scored on raw abundance.",
  "pickSoftThreshold fit indices per power; chosen marks the power used."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "module_building.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
